messages:
sana: hey — quick Q, trying to find the logs for request_id=rcq9f2a7. The trace link in the dashboard points to a span but the raw logs aren't showing up in Console. anyone have the fastest way to correlate req_id -> log lines from console or cli?

alex.m: two quick checks: 1) is this a sampled trace? if sampled=false the trace exists but might not have full span links. 2) check the request-id key format — we log as request_id=rcq9f2a7 everywhere? sometimes it's req_id or requestId.

sana: good point — this one comes from model-server, header was X-Req-Id and the app sets request_id in logs as request_id. I grepped the Kibana-esque Console UI and got nothing.

jordan: CLI is usually fastest for me: try the redwood cli (our internal tool) — example: `redwood logs query --service model-server --filter "request_id:rcq9f2a7" --since 60m`\.

cal: also if you have a trace_id you can use `redwood traces get --id <trace_id>` which will show span attributes including request_id keys and links to the raw log lines (span.meta.log_link). In Console: Observability -> Traces -> paste trace id -> open span -> click "Related logs".

ops-bot: deploy-bot noticed a recent rollout to model-server ~12m ago. If the request was during rollout there may be log retention lag on the old index. Status: rollout_complete.

sana: thanks. I ran `redwood logs query` and still blank. I do have the trace id (t-0a1b2c3d). Tried `redwood traces get --id t-0a1b2c3d` and see spans but no "request_id" attribute on the root span.

alex.m: okay — two more options: (A) search logs by trace_id directly: `redwood logs query --filter "trace_id:t-0a1b2c3d" --since 2h` — some services log trace_id instead of request_id; (B) if the service uses structured JSON logs try `redwood logs query --json --filter 'attributes.request_id=rcq9f2a7'`.

jordan: if CLI still fails, run a quick host-level grep on the node that served the request (only for oncall/infra folks): `ssh infra@node-xyz 'zcat /var/log/model-server/*.log.gz | rg "rcq9f2a7" || true'`. Useful when log shipping delayed.

cal: another explanation — our prefix cache can rewrite ids for internal router requests (we sometimes attach a router_req_id). Search for both patterns: `rcq9f2a7` and `router:rcq9f2a7` and check for `x-request-id` headers in span attributes.

sana: ran trace->logs search by trace_id: returned handful of logs from router but not model-server. The router logs include `router_req=router:rcq9f2a7` and a span attribute `peer.service: model-server` with `peer.request_id: rcq9f2a7-1`

alex.m: aha — looks like model-server appended a suffix. Try `redwood logs query --filter "request_id:rcq9f2a7" --or "request_id:rcq9f2a7-1"` or just wildcard: `--filter "request_id:rcq9f2a7*"`. Console search supports `request_id:rcq9f2a7*` too.

sana: that worked! found the entries in model-server with request_id=rcq9f2a7-1 and some stack traces. Thank you.

jordan: great. For future cases, tiny checklist: 1) try trace_id -> traces.get (find span attrs) 2) CLI logs query by trace_id and request_id variants 3) fallback to node grep if shipping lag 4) check for router suffixes/prefixes. I'll drop that checklist into the Observability runbook. :thumbsup:

cal: added a short note to the model-server logging README — include both request_id and trace_id in structured logs to avoid this.

sana: awesome. marking this resolved for now. if anyone sees follow-ups I'll open a ticket for standardizing the header mapping. :white_check_mark:
